newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, but recoup some losses.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, but recoup some losses.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended weaker after a volatile session on Monday, but they recouped most of their early losses after a rebound on Wall Street.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 39.77 points to close at 6655.32, after dropping 113 points at midday.
"Investors were fearful that the market sell-off would continue," said Montreal-based portfolio consultant Ron Meisels.
"When New York stated to turn around...cooler heads prevailed and started to do some shopping in Toronto as well," Meisels said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained nearly 109 points to finish at 7803 on Monday. The Dow sank 247 points on Friday.
Trading was moderate in Toronto with 79 million shares worth C$1.5 billion (US$1.1 billion) changing hands.
Canada's largest equities market usually has a delayed reaction to moves on Wall Street and will likely follow the Dow higher on Tuesday, Meisels predicted.
Many investors are eyeing the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday. The policy-setting group is expected to keep short-term U.S. interest rates steady.
All but one of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors lost ground. Conglomerates led the slide, followed by retail, media and golds. There was a 44-point gain in transportation.
Declining issues doubled advances 647 to 307 while another 311 stocks ended flat.
Investment company Harrowston Inc. topped most actives, dropping 0.30 to 4.75 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
Bombardier Inc., part of the industrial services sector, fell 2.80 to 29.55 in brisk trading.
Pacalta Resources Ltd. defied the sell off and jumped 2.30 to 21.50. The Calgary-based energy firm released details on two potentially big oil finds in Ecuador.
